claim: Realisation of means and instrument by adverbs is “extremely limited”. While treat surgically and communicate electronically are possible, “we could not replace the adverbs here with pharmaceutically or postally”.
evidence_summary: The audit reader found 23 PubMed title or abstract hits for pharmaceutically treated, including a verbal participle with a means reading: 1 200 769 patients pharmaceutically treated for their first occurrence of depression (Reps, Ryan and Rijnbeek 2021). The same search found no hits for the quoted phrases treated pharmaceutically and treat pharmaceutically. Postally wasn’t searched.
finding: A lead, not yet a finding. Preverbal pharmaceutically treated is attested in medical prose, but the postverbal order CGEL tests wasn’t found, so the claim may hold for treat pharmaceutically. A search of a general corpus for both orders would settle whether it needs qualifying.

evidence.passage: §2.2, p. 674. “we could not replace the adverbs here with pharmaceutically or postally”.
evidence.example: PubMed title and abstract searches for pharmaceutically treated, treated pharmaceutically and treat pharmaceutically.
evidence.establishes: A lead only. Preverbal uses occur; the postverbal order wasn’t found.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.

evidence.source: J. M. Reps, P. Ryan and P. R. Rijnbeek, “Investigating the impact of development and internal validation design when training prognostic models using a retrospective cohort in big US observational healthcare data”, BMJ Open 11(12): e050146 (2021).
evidence.example: “1 200 769 patients pharmaceutically treated for their first occurrence of depression.”
evidence.establishes: Preverbal pharmaceutically as a means modifier of treated in edited medical prose.
